extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners; patent applicants, agents, and attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner guidance for the form, content, execution, correction, and acceptance of oaths and declarations filed in U.S. utility and design patent applications (including foreign-executed oaths and continuation/divisional handling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath or Declaration Wording Cannot Be Amended
rubrics_metrics.description: The wording of an oath or declaration cannot be amended, altered or changed in any manner after it has been signed. If the wording is not correct or if all required affirmations have not been made, or if it has not been properly subscribed to, a new oath or declaration is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some deficiencies, however, can be corrected by a supplemental paper such as an application data sheet (see 37 CFR 1.76 and MPEP § 601.05) and a new oath or declaration is not necessary. Example: if the oath does not set forth evidence that the notary was acting within jurisdiction, a certificate of the notary may correct the deficiency. See MPEP §§ 602.01 and 602.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/Declaration Must Properly Identify the Application
rubrics_metrics.description: A new oath or declaration must properly identify the application of which it is to form a part, preferably by application number and filing date in the body of the oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should call attention to the requirement and give the reason when requiring a new oath. Any one of the combinations of information identified in MPEP § 602 as acceptable may be used. When filing a copy of a prior oath in a continuation/divisional after an application number is assigned, the cover letter should identify the new application number to avoid incorrect matching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must State 'Reviewed and Understands' the Application
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath/declaration must state that the person making it has reviewed and understands the contents of the specification, including the claims, as amended by any amendment specifically referred to in the oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omissions of this statement are defective and should be pointed out (form paragraph 6.05.05). The examiner must require remedy in the first Office action (see MPEP § 602.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Must State 'Original and First' Inventor(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath/declaration must state that the person making it believes the named inventor(s) to be the original and first inventor(s) of the subject matter which is claimed and for which a patent is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omission of this assertion is a defect to be raised (form paragraph 6.05.06). This is a statutory requirement and, if missing, a new oath/declaration is generally required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must Acknowledge Duty To Disclose (37 CFR 1.56)
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath/declaration must acknowledge the duty to disclose to the USPTO all information known to the person to be material to patentability as defined in 37 CFR 1.56.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oaths that fail to acknowledge the duty to disclose are defective (form paragraph 6.05.07). Note: earlier formulations referencing disclosure “material to the examination of the application in accordance with 37 CFR 1.56(a)” (pre-1992 wording) are no longer acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/Declaration Signature Must Be in Permanent Ink
rubrics_metrics.description: The signature (or oath/declaration) must be in permanent ink, or its equivalent in quality, as required under 37 CFR 1.52(a)(1)(iv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not in permanent ink, use form paragraph 6.32 and precede with form paragraph 6.05. This is a defect that the examiner should point out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Initialed/Non-Dated Alterations are Defective
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-initialed and/or non-dated alterations made to the oath or declaration are defects (see 37 CFR 1.52(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such alterations should be treated as defects and addressed using appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., 6.05.16). Examiner should require correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner Must Point Out Every Deficiency in First Office Action
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first Office action the examiner must point out every deficiency in a declaration or oath and require that the same be remedied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 6.05 to introduce one or more of form paragraphs 6.05.01–6.05.20 which explain specific errors (missing statements, improper execution, failure to reference earlier foreign application, improper identification of papers, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Some Defects May Be Corrected by an Application Data Sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain deficiencies in the oath/declaration may be corrected by filing an application data sheet (per 37 CFR 1.76 and MPEP § 601.05) instead of a new oath/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should inform applicant of the requirements of an application data sheet where relevant and indicate when a data sheet can cure the deficiency (e.g., identification issues). See examples in MPEP § 602.02 and form paragraph notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor Deficiencies May Be Waived by Examiner with Full Signatory Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner with full signatory authority may waive minor deficiencies in the body of the oath/declaration where the deficiencies are self-evidently cured in the rest of the oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If waived, the examiner should annotate the margin of the declaration/oath with reason for waiver, indicate application is ready for issue, and provide initials and date. Statutory requirements (e.g., citizenship, ‘original and first’ statement, administration before authorized person) cannot be waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute Declaration Required on Allowance to Correct Certain Defects
rubrics_metrics.description: When application is otherwise ready for issue but deficiencies remain that cannot be waived, applicant is required to submit a substitute declaration or oath to correct specified deficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The substitute must be filed within the THREE MONTH shortened statutory period set for reply in the Notice of Allowability (PTO-37). Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136 are not permitted. Failure to timely file results in abandonment. The transmittal should indicate the date of the Notice of Allowance and the application number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-Executed Oaths Must Be Properly Authenticated (Apostille/Consular)
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath executed in a foreign country must be properly authenticated in accordance with 37 CFR 1.66; e.g., include an apostille, a consular certificate, or certification of the position/authority of the officer signing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authority of the foreign officer is not certified, use form paragraphs 6.05 and 6.05.13. The Hague Apostille (where applicable) may be used in lieu of diplomatic/consular certification for member countries (see MPEP discussion and apostille model certificate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-Executed Oath — Papers Must Be Ribboned or Each Sheet Sealed
rubrics_metrics.description: When an oath is taken before a foreign officer, accompanying application papers (except drawings) must be attached together with a ribbon passed through all sheets and the ends brought together under the seal before affixing, or each sheet must be impressed with the official seal of the officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If papers are not properly ribboned or sealed, the case will be accepted for examination but before allowance duplicate compliant papers must be filed. Use form paragraphs 6.05 and 6.05.14 when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apostille Acceptable for Hague Convention Countries
rubrics_metrics.description: For member countries to the Hague Convention Abolishing the Requirement of Legalization, an apostille certifying the notary’s authority suffices in place of a diplomatic or consular certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP provides a link and guidance on locating member countries and shows the prescribed form for the apostille certificate. A declaration in lieu of application oath (37 CFR 1.68) still need not be ribboned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office No Longer Checks Date of Execution of Oath/Declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office no longer checks the date of execution of the oath or declaration and will not require a newly executed oath/declaration because the date is stale (more than 3 months prior) or omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants remain reminded of continuing duty of disclosure under 37 CFR 1.56 despite this change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation/Divisional May File Copy of Prior Oath/Declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation or divisional application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) (other than CIP) may be filed with a copy of the oath or declaration from the prior nonprovisional application; a copy may be submitted even if it identifies the prior application number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the copy is filed after the continuation/divisional has been assigned an application number, the cover letter should identify the continuation/divisional application number and indicate the oath is a copy of the prior application to avoid incorrect matching. Label the copy with the new application number in case cover letter is separated.

rubrics_metrics.name: If Continuation/Divisional Contains New Matter, Require New Oath and Surcharge and Redesignate as CIP
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner determines the continuation or divisional application contains new matter relative to the prior application, the examiner should notify applicant, require a new oath or declaration along with the surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f), and indicate that the application should be redesignated as a continuation-in-part (CIP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should inform applicant in the next Office action and take the two actions above (require new oath with surcharge and redesignate application).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Missing Inventor Signatures in Continuation/Divisional Filings
rubrics_metrics.description: If a copy of an oath/declaration submitted in a continuation/divisional omits the signature of one or more inventors, OPAP should send a 'Notice to File Missing Parts' requiring the signature of the nonsigning inventor unless a copy of the decision according 37 CFR 1.47 is included at filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If OPAP mails such a Notice, filing a copy of the decision granting 1.47 status with the applicable surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f) will be an acceptable reply. Alternatively, applicant may submit an oath/declaration signed by the previously nonsigning inventor together with the surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f) in reply to the Notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/Declaration Must Be Administered by Authorized Person; Statutory Requirements Non-Waivable
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory requirements — e.g., that the oath be administered before a person authorized to administer oaths or that the declaration contain required statutory language (35 U.S.C. § 25 language where applicable) — cannot be waived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these statutory conditions are not met, a new oath/declaration is required and waiver is not permissible; use form paragraph 6.46 when the application is otherwise allowable and a substitute is needed.
